lesson: Today, we work on sound. Sound means the way the consonants and vowels feel in your mouth and ear when you say the words out loud. Listen for three spots. The poem says, Cider brews of windfalls. Those hard D and W and F sounds slow your mouth down. It says, Hey, and the animal warmth of waiting. The W sound repeats and links the words. It says, Plain and unhurried. The soft open vowels make you say it slowly. This works because repeated sounds pull related words together. And hard sounds make you slow down. Your ear hears the pattern before your mind names it. That makes the lines feel settled, not rushed. Try this. Pick two or three words near each other and give them the same starting sound. The second time through, say the words quietly with your mouth and seal where the sound slow you down. Then hear, so, up, break that slowness.
